title: Real-World: User Login
story: The login screen is the gatekeeper of your app. Username empty? Password too short? Wrong credentials? Every failure needs a clear response. Write the logic that guards the door — and tells users exactly why they can't get in.
why: Login validation is the classic real-world Result use case — multiple checks on multiple fields, each with distinct error messages, chained into one clean function.
analogy: Login validation is like a bouncer at a club — they check your ID (username not empty), your age (password length), and the guest list (credentials match). Fail any check and you're not getting in.
try_it: Add a rate limiter: `login_attempts` counter. If the same username fails 3 times, return Err("Account locked. Too many attempts."). Test with 4 failed logins for the same user.
tips: Check the simplest conditions first — empty fields are cheaper to check than credential matching
Return early on each validation failure — the function stops at the first problem found
Keep credential checks separate from format validation — it makes the logic clearer
common_mistakes: Revealing too much in error messages — 'User not found' tells hackers the username exists, use 'Invalid credentials'
Checking password length AFTER checking credentials — the format is wrong regardless of whether the password matches
Using == for password comparison in real code — but for this exercise, it's fine; real systems use hashing
